study: Newman et al. 2012, Alabama Math, Science & Technology Initiative (AMSTI) teacher PD, grades 4-8 RCT, one-year effects (NCEE 2012-4008)
eval_evidence: IES/NCEE evaluation (NCEE 2012-4008) prepared by Empirical Education Inc. and REL Southeast; a third-party/contractor evaluation with no AMSTI developer stake.
developer_evidence: AMSTI is the Alabama state initiative delivered through the state/AMSTI regional infrastructure (summer PD, in-school support, materials); the evaluation team (Empirical Education/REL) did not deliver the PD. Treated as the school system / state program delivering, not the research/eval team.
cascade_evidence: Report does not clearly specify the developer->trainer->teacher transmission structure for the AMSTI summer PD and in-school support (state-program delivery); hops not stated, so unclear.
counterfactual_evidence: Matched-pair control schools assigned to a business-as-usual control for Year 1 (the uncontaminated TPD-vs-BAU wave); controls entered AMSTI only in Year 2.
coaching_evidence: AMSTI = summer PD (institute) plus 'in-school support' / access to materials during the year; the design centers on summer training with periodic in-school support, not recurring (monthly+) in-class coaching cycles -> occasional.
student_dose_evidence: AMSTI provides teacher PD plus hands-on materials/manipulatives for the teacher to use; only the teacher's own math/science instruction changes. No tutoring/pull-out/added-minutes/software dose delivered directly to students.
maturity_evidence: The only uncontaminated TPD-vs-BAU contrast extracted is the END-OF-YEAR-1 (first implementation year) effect; teachers in their first year of AMSTI. (Two-year effects excluded because control entered AMSTI in Year 2.)
